title: Drift-aware compressed KV cache experiments (layer-adaptive FP8/INT8/INT4)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Evaluate a drift-aware, layer-adaptive compression strategy for the KV cache that reduces GPU memory footprint while bounding semantic degradation for production workloads. This ticket defines experiment design, datasets, metrics, and the runtime validation harness for FP8/INT8/INT4 mixes that vary by layer and token-cohort. The novelty is a lightweight online drift detector that adjusts per-layer quantization tiers and an introspective rollback mechanism that triggers full-precision re-evaluation for requests with high fidelity risk. We will measure both micro (logit/cosine/perplexity) and macro (QA/summary fidelity and hallucination) impacts and quantify memory and latency trade-offs across serving modes (hosted, dedicated, private).
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by ML infra and runtime leads
Experimental harness that can replay production traces with quantization injection is implemented
Benchmarks run on at least 3 representative models (e.g., LlamaX-13B, Redwood-Open-7B, Falcon-40B) and reported
Measured memory savings and latency charts for continuous-batching workloads produced
A gating rule (semantic fidelity delta < 1.5% on primary QA set) specified for rollout decision
PRs created for runtime changes and linked to this ticket
tasks: Implement per-layer quantization operator in runtime with switchable FP32/FP16/FP8/INT8/INT4 paths
Build trace replay harness with token-level timing and KV state reconstruction
Define cohorts and drift detector thresholds using rolling-window cosine statistics
Run dense parameter sweep for layer-bit allocations and record latency/memory/quality
Integrate an introspective rollback API: mark request for replay on full-precision if fidelity risk > threshold
Create visual dashboard for semantic fidelity delta, token-level error maps, and memory savings

risks: FP8 kernel support varies across cloud GPU types: fallback to slower FP16/FP32 may negate memory savings
Quantization may disproportionately affect rare-token cohorts leading to increased hallucination in low-data domains
Rollback/replay increases tail-latency for affected requests if not rate-limited
Metrics like perplexity understate semantic shifts; need downstream task evaluations
mitigations: Add per-cohort conservative defaults and a gradual rollout starting with non-SLA customers
Implement rate-limited rollback and sampling-based full-precision re-eval to bound latency impact
Expose operator-level telemetry on quantization error to Console for early detection
Provide recommendation engine to suggest layer budgets based on model and trace statistics
next_steps: Open formal RFC for runtime API changes and invite runtime/perf/ML infra owners
If QA delta < 1.5% on primary devsets, schedule a canary on Dedicated in cycle 2025-W09
